policy: per PROTOCOL v1.0 §2.4 + gap analysis Finding 5: preserved != trusted. A corpus's directory placement (published/, ground-truth/, etc.) does NOT confer authority. Two orthogonal axes govern the gate: verification_status (is the source / citation retrievable?) and reference_eligibility (may this corpus satisfy an independent-reference validation gate for calendar correctness?). The gate requires VERIFIED + ELIGIBLE. Anything else fails closed.

verification_status.UNVERIFIED: the citation could not be independently verified from this host (book not held, ISBN not retrievable, page cannot be cross-checked, etc.)
verification_status.VERIFIED: the source has been fetched / the citation has been confirmed against a retrievable record (the source itself may still be non-authoritative — see reference_eligibility)

reference_eligibility.INELIGIBLE: the corpus may inform the work but cannot satisfy an independent-reference validation gate, even if VERIFIED. reasons include: practitioner / non-academic source, source does not actually cover the claimed calendrical relationship, source is older than the regime it claims to describe.
reference_eligibility.ELIGIBLE: the corpus may satisfy an independent-reference validation gate for calendar correctness

authority_basis.scholarly: academic publication, peer-reviewed or from a recognized scholarly press
authority_basis.customary: attested by a Balinese customary authority (pemangku, bendesa, etc.)
authority_basis.institutional: attested by a state institution (university, ministry, heritage body)
authority_basis.practitioner: practitioner calendar (commercial or community) — may be VERIFIED but is generally INELIGIBLE for authoritative calendar validation
authority_basis.software_reference: a software implementation that itself cites a verifiable source (the source is what matters, not the software)
authority_basis.unknown: the basis could not be classified — UNVERIFIED by default

separation_from_ceremonial_tiers: this status governs the bibliographic / evidence-chain layer for conformance corpora. It does NOT affect Dewata's ceremonial/record provenance tiers (computed / registered / predicted / verified) governed by PROTOCOL §2.6. A corpus's verification_status: VERIFIED does NOT imply 'verified' in the ceremonial provenance ladder.

enforcement: Cross-validation machinery (phase-1/src/dewatacalendar/cross_validation.py and conformance.py) and CLI (cli.py) MUST call can_satisfy_validation_gate() before claiming any corpus satisfies an independent-reference validation gate. The cross_validation module annotates outcomes with _corpus_verification_status, _corpus_reference_eligibility, _corpus_authority_basis, and _corpus_legacy_status so downstream consumers cannot accidentally treat unverified or ineligible data as authoritative.
